### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, touching **31** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/cli/README.md`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**21** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9360df4138615a646630c0727c3b975711fb2eb1`.

⛔ **4** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/cli/README.md`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `objectName (symbol, 37 pages)`
- **13** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **26** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9360df4138615a646630c0727c3b975711fb2eb1` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `ef83797d0dd30393701d31f289816c77b6cf7130` — the merge of head `c0190c97429a215c3badeca6a828b5943860056a` into base `9360df4138615a646630c0727c3b975711fb2eb1`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin ef83797d0dd30393701d31f289816c77b6cf7130 && git checkout ef83797d0dd30393701d31f289816c77b6cf7130
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 9360df4138615a646630c0727c3b975711fb2eb1 c0190c97429a215c3badeca6a828b5943860056a && git checkout -B drift-repro 9360df4138615a646630c0727c3b975711fb2eb1 && git merge --no-ff c0190c97429a215c3badeca6a828b5943860056a

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9360df4138615a646630c0727c3b975711fb2eb1
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 9360df4138615a646630c0727c3b975711fb2eb1` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `c0190c97429a215c3badeca6a828b5943860056a`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card #21325 body and comments `5945870485` (direction), `5946394138` (claim), `5947877777` (os-dev-report); PR #21369 body and its 19-file list; `git diff 5fd4855a9ae7c24f31070227131f2eb42037aabb refs/review/pr-21369`; the readers by sha at the head (`packages/cli/src/commands/generate.ts` at base and head, `packages/metadata/src/view-container.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/view-container-name-refusal.ts`, `packages/spec/liveness/view.json`, `packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts` at `expandViewContainerWithDiagnostics`, `packages/cli/src/commands/lint.ts` `lintConfig`, `packages/lint/src/authoring-rules.ts`, `validate-list-view-field-refs.ts`, `services/service-automation/src/engine.ts` `flowStatusDisabled`, `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs`, `scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs`); check-runs on the head collapsed latest-per-name: 35 runs, 33 success, 2 skipped (`Console Pin Gate`, `Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)`), 0 failure, 0 pending — verified, matches dispatch. The state of #21310 (closed 2026-10-02T07:46Z) and #21370 (open) was read from the API to settle two boundary flags.

### ① Derived judgments

**(a) Bindings never derived from the item's name — right, for every reference each scaffold writes.** At the head each generator declares `binds` and `runMetadataGeneration` calls the pure `resolveScaffoldBindings` after the config load, the namespace read and the residual-prefix gate, and before `dir`, the render, the parse check and the dry-run branch. The references enumerated from the templates: `view` writes `object`, every `columns[].field` and the `sort` field — all from the binding read off the loaded stack (`stackBindingCandidates`), the view being named after a declared object (`binds.object: 'name'`) and refused when the stack does not declare it; `flow` writes the start node `config.objectName` from `--object` or the stack's only object; `action` writes `objectName` from `--object` or the only object and `target` from `--flow` or the only flow; `app` writes `navigation[0].objectName` and its label from the bound object. No template reads `objectNameFor(name, …)` for a binding any more; `requireBinding` throws when a binding scaffold is rendered without one, and the per-PR pin asserts both that the bound object lands and that the namespace-prefixed item name appears nowhere in the artifact. `dashboard`, `skill`, `object`, `picklist` bind nothing (verified in their templates). The non-interactive reading of "or from the stack's existing objects" — exactly one declared binds, several refuses and lists them — is right: no `os generate` path prompts and the card's own Expected says "asks / takes `--object`". **`--flow` is within the direction.** The direction's prohibition is on any reference derived from the new item's name; the action's flow (`NAME_flow`) was one, and the alternative (a script action with an invented body, or an action bound to a flow nobody declared, which `defineStack` passed when no flows existed) would have kept the defect on the second reference. It is spelled exactly like `--object` (long flag, value, default = the stack's only one), the dev flagged it in the report's `argument_shape` and in the PR body, and the changeset and `cli.mdx` carry it. A second public flag of the same shape, applied to the same rule, did not need a separate ruling; the judgment is recorded here.

**(b) Refusals — right: loud, remedy named, nothing written.** All five routes land in `refuseGeneration` (printError, the body, `process.exit(1)`): no `--object` with zero or several objects, `--object` or `--flow` naming nothing declared, no `--flow` with zero or several flows, a view named after an undeclared object, and a binding scaffold outside a project (`project.kind !== 'loaded'`). Each prints the declared names where there are any and the next command to run. `unusedBindingFlagRefusal` runs in `Generate.run` before the `SUB_COMMANDS` routing, so `--object` or `--flow` on `object`, `dashboard`, `skill`, `picklist`, `view` (names its object), `flow` (`--flow`), `app` (`--flow`), `types`, `client` and `migration` is refused rather than silently honoured; an unknown type still gets the roster answer. Every refusal sits above the first write, and the spawned pin asserts a byte-identical tree. One nit, not a defect: the "declares none" branches do not restate the empty list in the body — the headline says it.

**(c) View container `name` and `label` both dropped, `list.label` written — right, checked against the readers.** `deriveViewContainerObject` (view-container.ts) returns `own object ?? list.data.object ?? form.data.object ?? name`, so with `object` set `name` is never the registry key. `viewContainerNameRefusal` returns `undefined` when `name` is absent or empty and refuses only a `name` that is set and differs from that key; its remedy text is "drop `name`, or set it to the key". The liveness ledger grades `name` `dead` ("a copy nobody reads") and `label` `dead` with the exact evidence the dev cites: `expandViewContainerWithDiagnostics` stamps each expanded item with `v.label` / `defaultList.label` / `defaultForm.label` and never `container.label`, and Studio drops containers from every view list. `object` is `live`. So the old template's comment ("the server refuses a container whose `name` disagrees") and `os validate`'s "dead" were both true and compatible, exactly as the dev wrote. `lintConfig` reads the view label through `getViewLabel` and requires it (`required/label`), so `list.label` is the surviving label. Columns are every declared field (`ListColumnSchema.width` is optional; `list-view-field-unknown` / `-dotted` cannot fire on a declared, undotted name), sort uses `resolveDisplayField` only when it names a declared field. `scaffold-wiring.ts` `registeredItemName` keeps the reach report finding a nameless container under `deriveViewContainerObject`; the `@objectstack/metadata/view-container` subpath is exported and `@objectstack/metadata` is a declared CLI dependency.

**(d) Pin family close-out — right.** `generate-scaffold-validates.test.ts` iterates `GENERATOR_SCAFFOLD_TARGETS` (derived from `GENERATORS`), builds each kind's prerequisites from its own `binds` (object stem `probe_target`, flow stem `probe_target_changed`, deliberately not the item name), resolves them through `stackBindingCandidates`, and `findings()` collects: the `defineStack` load error, `lintUnknownStackKeys` + `lintUnknownAuthoringKeys`, `safeParse` issues, `runAuthoringRules('validate')` and `('build')` at every severity, and `lintConfig` (the command's own checks plus its `runAuthoringRules('lint')` pass at line 680) at every severity — then `toEqual([])`. The ledger `KNOWN_UNVALIDATED_SCAFFOLDS` is empty. A kind added later with `binds` of `object`/`flow` or none is measured with no edit; a kind binding a key outside `ScaffoldBinds` fails the roster test loudly naming the stem to add. The nightly `generate-scaffold-gates.e2e.test.ts` runs one fresh on-ramp starter per kind plus a CONTROL leg, chains prerequisites from `binds`, runs `os validate|build|lint --json` (shapes verified: `errors`/`warnings` with `rule`/`path`; lint `issues`; `os build` is an alias of `compile`, which writes `dist/objectstack.json`), requires exit 0 and zero findings beyond `STARTER_LATENT_FINDINGS`, which has one entry (`field-no-consumers@objects[0].fields.body`). It goes red when the starter is fixed (the "still fires somewhere" test) and cannot cover a scaffold's own object (the finding's object must be one the bare starter declares, read from the compiled artifact). Evidence of the nightly's green is the dev's run (69 tests); it is not in per-PR CI by its tier, as its sibling `generate-scaffolds-reach-stack.e2e.test.ts` is not. `generate-binds-from-stack.test.ts` pins every resolver and unused-flag branch on named subjects.

**(e) Published text — every factual sentence true at the head.** `cli.mdx` Quick Start runs on `npm create objectstack` (blank starter: one object `note`, no flows): after `os generate object customer` two objects exist, so `--object customer` is needed; `customer_changed` yields `customer_changed_flow`, the only flow, so `os generate action approve --object customer` "runs the stack's only flow" — true. The `#### os generate` region: the binding sources, the four refusals, "outside a project … refused", "`--object` and `--flow` on a type that takes neither are refused rather than ignored", the options, the examples (`os g app sales --object customer`, `os g action escalate --object customer --flow customer_changed_flow`), step 1 of "What it does", and the rewritten "Refused" bullet all match the resolver at the head. Typical Workflow `os g flow opportunity_changed --object opportunity` after four objects — true. `packages/cli/README.md` Quick Start: `os init my-app` declares `my_app_item`, then `os generate object task` makes two objects, so `os generate view task` (named after declared `my_app_task`) and `os generate flow task_changed --object task` — true; the Typical Workflow line `os generate view customer` after `os generate object customer` still holds. The changeset's statements (prefix lookup, only-object default, the refusal list including `types`/`client`/`migration`, object drops `description`, view drops `name`/`label` and gains `list.label` plus all fields, flow `status: 'active'` — `flowStatusDisabled` is exactly `obsolete || invalid` — action `locations: ['record_header']` in the schema vocabulary, app nav label) are each true. Sweep for `os g|generate flow|action|app|view` across `content/docs`, `packages/cli/README.md`, `packages/create-objectstack/src/templates/**`, `skills/**`: no other invocation; `getting-started/your-first-project.mdx:143` is a generic mention; the blank starter's `README.md:43`/`:74`, `objectstack.config.ts:49`/`:70` and the `src/*/index.ts` barrel comments use a `NAME` placeholder and stay true for a declared name (an undeclared one is now refused with the remedy named), so nothing published is left false.

### ② Semver level

Right. `@objectstack/cli: minor` with a BREAKING banner, `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, and exactly one ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. The arm: the flags widen the public surface, but the same diff narrows the accept set — `os g flow X` in a multi-object stack, `os g action X` with no flow, any binding scaffold outside a project, and the pre-change `cli.mdx` examples are now refused — and the declaration takes at most one arm, so the breaking arm is the honest one; the claim's expected `(widening)` was the pre-diff guess and the dev re-measured as the claim required. Level: `(narrowing)` is BREAKING; `check-changeset-no-major` forbids `major` during the launch window, so `minor` is the only correct grade. ADR-0087 disposition: no authorable key, export or stored shape moves and files generated by earlier releases load unchanged, so there is nothing for `objectstack migrate meta` to rewrite; the body's "What to write instead" is command usage, not a consumer-code rewrite, and the gate (`Check Changeset`, `Lint & Repo Gates`) accepted it. The migration-sentence requirement is met by that section.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **cli.mdx edited outside the `#### os generate` region (Quick Start, Typical Workflow)** — accepted. Both blocks were falsified by this diff (each is refused on the starter it documents); the os-dev rule requires fixing text a change falsifies; neither block is in `### Quality` (#21323's region).
- **Per-kind literal zero held on the scaffold's own output; the starter's latent warning ledgered** — accepted. The per-PR pin asserts literal zero with no ledger; the nightly's one-entry ledger is shrink-only, must sit on a starter-declared object, and must still fire, so it cannot absorb a scaffold finding and turns red when the template is fixed. The residual is the starter's `note.body`, not something `os g` writes; filed as #21370 (verified open, names both templates).
- **Two CLI internals (`project-namespace.ts` carries `config` on the loaded result; `scaffold-wiring.ts` `registeredItemName`)** — accepted: internals `generate.ts` directly references, inside the claim's wording.
- **Nine existing tests updated** — accepted after reading each diff: every change hands a binding or a flag; `unimportable-alias` moves its cases to `dashboard`/`skill` (still two generators, same layer); `stack-reach` gains a flow control and asserts the written `objectName`/`target`; `namespace-prefix` adds a pin that a binding template writes exactly what it is handed; nothing weakened.
- **README fixed in the patch round** — accepted. #21310 closed at 07:46Z; the README commit `c0190c97` is 08:15Z; `No other open PR may claim the same single-writer path` is green. One correction for the dispatching seat: the PR body's Acceptance notes still say `packages/cli/README.md` "was not edited" (body updated 08:16Z) — stale against the file list; fix the sentence, not the diff.
- **run-dev.js serving dist** — accepted as noted: test infrastructure with no public door, recorded in the PR's Acceptance notes; the dev reran spawned suites against a dist built from the head and redid E1 as a dist ablation.
- **Blank starter README line 43** — accepted as noted, not filed: the sentence stays true for a declared `NAME` and an undeclared one is refused with the remedy named, so it is a precision gap on a template outside the surface, not a trap. It appears only in the os-dev-report's `out_of_scope_findings`, not in the PR's Acceptance notes; minor.
- **`--flow`** — see ①(a): within the direction, flagged by the dev, no ruling owed.
- **`Fixes #21325`** — right to close on this PR. All three cases on the card are fixed and pinned (per-PR and nightly), the Expected ("passes `os validate` AND `os lint` … targets real metadata (or asks / takes `--object`)") is met for every kind's output, and the one remaining warning is the starter's own defect with its own card. `The card this PR closes must claim this branch` and `Part-of PR must not also close its card` are both green.
